PraxisKind.description:
The five praxis types, mirroring the vault's own vocabulary.

Kept in lock-step with :class:`creek.models.PraxisType`, which is what a
``04-Praxis/`` page's ``praxis_type`` is actually constrained to;
:mod:`creek_mcp.compiled_pages` withholds any page naming something outside
it, so a wire enum that drifted would refuse a legitimate page on the way
out — or, worse, admit a hand-edited value the vault never sanctioned.
``tests/test_adepthood_contract_models.py`` pins the two lists equal.

Attributes:
    COMMITMENT: A promise the writer has made.
    FRAMEWORK: A way of seeing they reuse.
    HABIT: Something done repeatedly, near-automatically.
    INSIGHT: A distilled realisation.
    PRACTICE: Something done deliberately and returned to.
PraxisKind.title: PraxisKind

PraxisLifecycle.description:
The four praxis lifecycle statuses, mirroring :class:`creek.models.PraxisStatus`.

Attributes:
    ACTIVE: Currently being practised.
    INTEGRATED: Absorbed; no longer needs deliberate attention.
    PROPOSED: Named but not yet taken up.
    RELEASED: Deliberately let go.
PraxisLifecycle.title: PraxisLifecycle

RelatedEddy.description:
One eddy the reflected entry belongs to (contract 0.9, #873).

Carries the same compiled-page caveat as :class:`RelatedPraxis`, and one
more that is specific to it: ``description`` and ``fragment_count`` are
*synthesised from the eddy's members*, so publishing the page to a caller
admitted to only some of them would hand over a summary of content they
cannot read. :mod:`creek_mcp.compiled_pages` therefore admits an eddy only
when the members it can enumerate account for ``fragment_count`` exactly
**and** every one of them is within the ceiling.

Attributes:
    title: The eddy page's title.
    description: The eddy's own one-line description; ``""`` when the page
        declares none.
    fragment_count: How many fragments the eddy clusters. A tally, so never
        negative.
    formed: The ``YYYY-MM-DD`` the eddy was first detected.

description.description: The eddy's own description; may be empty.
description.title: Description

formed.description: ISO date the eddy was first detected.
formed.title: Formed

fragment_count.description: How many fragments the eddy clusters.
fragment_count.title: Fragment Count

RelatedEddy.title: RelatedEddy

RelatedPraxis.description:
One praxis page the reflected entry contributed to (contract 0.9, #873).

**Compiled, not raw.** A praxis page is distilled *from* fragments, so it
is published only when every id in its ``derived_from`` resolves to a
fragment within the caller's ceiling — and withheld outright when its
provenance cannot be enumerated in full. That rule lives in
:mod:`creek_mcp.compiled_pages`; nothing on this model re-derives it, and
no field here carries a tier, because a page that reached the wire is one
whose whole provenance was already admitted.

Attributes:
    title: The praxis page's title.
    praxis_type: Which of the five :class:`PraxisKind` values it is.
    status: Where it sits in the :class:`PraxisLifecycle`.
    excerpt: The page's own opening prose, whitespace-collapsed and capped
        at :data:`creek_mcp.compiled_pages.EXCERPT_CHARS`. Not a model
        summary and not grounding-checked — it is the page as written.

excerpt.description: The page's own opening prose, capped.
excerpt.title: Excerpt

praxis_type.description: Which kind of praxis this is.

status.description: Where it sits in its lifecycle.

RelatedPraxis.title: RelatedPraxis

RelatedThread.description:
One narrative thread the entry belongs to (contract 0.36, #2127).

A thread page is compiled from the fragments that link to it, exactly as
an eddy is, so it carries :class:`RelatedEddy`'s caveat:
:mod:`creek_mcp.compiled_pages` names a thread only when one of the
entry's seed fragments is a member, the members it can enumerate account
for the page's ``fragment_count``, and every one of them is within the
caller's ceiling. Only these three labels cross the wire — never the
page's body, description or member count.

Attributes:
    id: The thread page's own ``id``.
    title: The thread page's title.
    status: :class:`ThreadLifecycle`, from the subfolder it lives in.
RelatedThread.title: RelatedThread

ReplyVoice.description:
Which voice a letter or reflection was written in (#2126).

The wire twin of :class:`creek.author.reply_voice.ReplyVoice`, which this
framework-free module does not import; a test pins the two vocabularies
equal.

Attributes:
    OWNER: The prompt carried the owner's own style, drawn only from the
        owner's own writing: owner-authored style skills, register samples
        admitted at the caller's ceiling, or the voice fingerprint.
    HIGHER_SELF: No owner style was found; the generic Higher Self voice.
ReplyVoice.title: ReplyVoice

ThreadLifecycle.description:
The three thread statuses, mirroring :class:`creek.models.ThreadStatus`.

Read from the ``02-Threads/`` subfolder a thread page lives in (#2127).

Attributes:
    ACTIVE: A current that is still running.
    DORMANT: Quiet for now, not over.
    RESOLVED: A current that has run its course.
ThreadLifecycle.title: ThreadLifecycle

VoiceDraftAttribution.description:
The fixed attribution of every remotely stored Voice Draft.

All three fields are literals with defaults, so a producer can construct
the one valid value with no caller input and a consumer cannot mistake an
AI-authored draft for owner voice.

author.description: Always AI; owner authorship is inexpressible.
author.title: Author

voice_weight.description: Always zero; the draft never trains the owner's voice.
voice_weight.title: Voice Weight

VoiceDraftAttribution.title: VoiceDraftAttribution

WireTierCeiling.description:
The only two tier ceilings expressible on ``/v1``.

``/v1`` is remote by construction, and
:func:`creek_mcp.policy.admitted_ceiling` refuses any remote call declaring
a ceiling outside :data:`creek_mcp.policy.REMOTE_ADMITTED_CEILINGS` *before
dispatch*. Since #1073 that decision is transport-neutral, so every adapter
is meant to reach it the same way; the MCP surface does so today through
:meth:`creek_mcp.server._BoundedFastMCP.call_tool`, and #1074 mounts the
``/v1`` handlers that will. This enum mirrors that frozenset, so
``intimate`` and ``all`` are not merely refused at runtime — they cannot be
constructed at all, which is the half of the guarantee that does not depend
on a handler remembering to ask.

The same two values double as the wire's *tier* vocabulary (see
:class:`JournalUpsertRequest`, :class:`JournalUpsertResponse` and
:class:`ReflectionResponse`). The two vocabularies coincide by
construction: the set of tiers a remote caller may name is exactly the set
of ceilings a remote caller may declare, because a tier above the remote
cap is one no remote request can reach in either direction.

Attributes:
    OPEN: Openly publishable content only (ontology §13.2).
    PERSONAL: Adds personal — and, per #961, ``unclassified`` — content.
WireTierCeiling.title: WireTierCeiling

description:
The letter the vault wrote, and the Voice Draft now holding it.

Attributes:
    status: Always ``"ok"``. Failure is an :class:`ErrorEnvelope`, and an
        acute-distress entry is a :class:`CareEscalationResponse`.
    tier_ceiling: The caller's declared ceiling, echoed.
    external_id: The caller-owned id; ``DELETE
        /v1/voice-drafts/{external_id}`` retracts the letter.
    fragment_id: The stable vault-side fragment identity.
    action: ``created`` for a new letter, ``unchanged`` when the id already
        held one, which is returned as stored without a model call.
    tier: The stored letter's tier.
    title: The stored title.
    letter: The letter text. Free model prose, never a verbatim quote. A
        new letter is capped at :data:`MAX_LETTER_CHARS`; an ``unchanged``
        one is returned exactly as stored, so a draft put by
        ``PUT /v1/voice-drafts`` is never truncated on the way out.
    attribution: Fixed AI attribution and zero voice weight.
    inference_source: The route that answered, one of ``pool:creek``,
        ``pool:attested:<vendor>``, ``request_key:<vendor>`` or ``local``
        (ADR-0016 Decision 1 item 11). Since contract 0.19, and omitted
        for a caller declaring an earlier minor. Also omitted — rather
        than guessed — on an answer this vocabulary does not label, which
        today is an operator's own cloud key on a self-hosted vault or an
        attested enclave (unreadable, and still off-device). The
        consumer's use for the field is to notice a route it did not
        expect, so a label the server cannot stand behind would be worse
        than none.
    voice: Which voice the letter was written in (#2126): ``owner`` when
        the owner's own style shaped it, ``higher_self`` otherwise. An
        ``unchanged`` letter reports the voice it was stored with, and a
        letter stored before contract 0.35 is ``higher_self``. Since
        contract 0.35, and omitted for a caller declaring an earlier minor.
    related_praxis: At most three :class:`RelatedPraxis` the letter's
        source entry touches (#2127), selected and admitted exactly as on
        :class:`ReflectionResponse`.
    related_eddies: At most two :class:`RelatedEddy`, the same way.
    related_threads: At most two :class:`RelatedThread`, the same way.
        Each of the three is absent when nothing qualifies, and for a
        caller declaring a minor below
        :data:`RELATED_SURFACES_SINCE_MINOR`.

action.description: Created, or unchanged when the id already held a letter.
action.title: Action

attribution.description: Fixed AI attribution and zero voice weight.

inference_source.description: Route that answered: pool:creek, pool:attested:<vendor>, request_key:<vendor> or local. Since contract 0.19.
inference_source.title: Inference Source

letter.description: The letter text; free model prose.
letter.title: Letter

related_eddies.description: Eddies the source entry belongs to; absent when none. Since 0.36.
related_eddies.title: Related Eddies

related_praxis.description: Praxis the source entry touches; absent when none. Since 0.36.
related_praxis.title: Related Praxis

related_threads.description: Threads the entry belongs to; absent when none. Since contract 0.36.
related_threads.title: Related Threads

status.description: Always ok; failure is an error.
status.title: Status

voice.description: owner when the owner's own style shaped the text, else higher_self. Since contract 0.35.

title: LetterResponse
